name: lexsync: Lexical optimisation and hardware-timed experiment generation
description: A cross-platform, dual-language (R and Python) toolkit that unifies many-language lexical-corpus access, parallel multidimensional stimulus matching, counterbalancing, item resampling, deterministic pseudoword generation and the automated generation of hardware-timed PsychoPy, OpenSesame and jsPsych experiment scripts. The R and Python engines select byte-identical stimuli, and every run ships a machine- and human-readable materials datasheet (provenance, checksums, realised control). The MIT licence covers the source code only; the example lexica bundled in both packages are derived from wordfreq (Speer, 2022) and are distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0, whose terms and required attribution are recorded in LICENSE-DATA and corpora/ATTRIBUTION.md.
citation: See CITATION.cff. A manuscript describing lexsync is in preparation.
